keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row starts in 1429. Before that it draws the same cells inside other rows: House of Luxembourg to 1414, County of Brabant 1415-1421 (43 of 45 cells in 1420) and Duchy of Bavaria 1422-1428 (44 of 45 cells in 1428). The Duchy page says 'In 1411, Sigismund of Luxembourg lost the duchy to his niece Elisabeth because he defaulted on a loan'; her husbands Anthony of Brabant (to 1415) and John III of Bavaria (to 1425) shared the rule. The dossiers of Brabant and Bavaria already take these cells out of their outlines. The 1429 outline is used for 1411-1428; the pages give no extent.

10.1 k km2 for 1429-1430, 44 cells; one cell short of the 1431 outline. The Duchy page infobox gives no area, so no ratio can be taken. The page lists the ducal lands as 'formed in 1353 by integration of the old County of Luxembourg'.
10.3 k km2 (45 cells), the same cells as the 1440 shape. No infobox area; no event on the pages opened moves the border in 1431-1442.

correction.text: unchanged outline of the duchy, holding 1440-1443 only: 'In 1443, the duchy passed to Duke Philip the Good of Burgundy'

keyframe_review.note: Years only: the outline is right but ends in 1443, not 1449. From 1443 the land is the Duke of Burgundy's (infobox 'Held by the Dukes of Burgundy: 1443'); Cliopatria's Duchy of Burgundy shape covers the same 44 cells from 1450, leaving 1444-1449 to this row. The duchy as a title lasted to 1795 (Duchy page) inside the Burgundian and Habsburg Netherlands.

region.text: the duchy of Luxembourg, lost by Sigismund to his niece Elisabeth

ledger.note: 1411: Elisabeth of Görlitz takes the duchy of Luxembourg from her uncle Sigismund. 'In 1411, Sigismund of Luxembourg lost the duchy to his niece Elisabeth because he defaulted on a loan.' The duchy is older ('in 1354, Emperor Charles IV elevated it to the status of a duchy for his brother Wenceslaus'); the dossier starts where the duchy leaves the House of Luxembourg row (Cliopatria, to 1414) and before Cliopatria's own row (1429).

region.text: the duchy of Luxembourg, passed to Duke Philip the Good of Burgundy

ledger.note: 1443: Philip the Good of Burgundy takes Luxembourg. 'In 1443, the duchy passed to Duke Philip the Good of Burgundy.' Elizabeth page: in a treaty she let Philip administer the duchy 'immediately' and inherit it on her death, then he broke the agreement 'two years later' by a night attack and her forces were expelled; her titular claim runs 1443-1451.

1443: the duchy of Luxembourg ceases to be a state of its own and joins the lands of the Dukes of Burgundy (infobox 'Held by the Dukes of Burgundy: 1443'; 'To Habsburg: 1482'); the title survives inside the Burgundian and Habsburg Netherlands.

wars.name: Burgundian takeover of Luxembourg
wars.outcome: Philip the Good broke his earlier agreement with Elisabeth by a night attack and expelled her; 'In 1443, the duchy passed to Duke Philip the Good of Burgundy'.
wars.note: Elizabeth page: the treaty let Philip administer the duchy 'immediately' and inherit it; the attack came 'two years later'. William III of Saxony is listed as a claimant 1439-1482 on the Duchy page; no fighting is dated for his claim.

certainty.note: No treaty line or survey is dated on the pages opened; the outline is Cliopatria's single 45-cell shape.

notes: Scope: Cliopatria's row is 1429-1449 (3 shapes, the same 45 cells); this dossier runs 1411-1443 on the two pages' dates (1411 Elisabeth; 1443 Philip the Good). Before 1429 the same cells sit inside House of Luxembourg (to 1414), County of Brabant (1415-1421) and Duchy of Bavaria (1422-1428), and the Brabant and Bavaria dossiers already take Luxembourg out of their outlines; the house-of-luxembourg dossier should end its Luxembourg lands at 1410. After 1443 the land is Burgundian (Cliopatria's Burgundy shape from 1450, Habsburg Monarchy from 1490); 1444-1449 stay in this Cliopatria row but are dropped here. The duchy as a title continued to 1795 (Duchy page: 'annexed by the French First Republic' on 1 October 1795), and the Grand Duchy 'Luxembourg' (Cliopatria 1890-2024, slug luxembourg) shares Wikidata Q2719360 but is a different state 450 years later, so no merge is made. The duchy's 1354 elevation and 1353 formation (Duchy page) are not drawn: no page gives its extent then. The Duchy page infobox lists Elizabeth of Görlitz for both 1415-1419 and 1425-1443 and gives no area; William III of Saxony is a claimant 1439-1482. The first Elizabeth URL (Elisabeth_of_Görlitz) returned not found. Not entered for lack of a page: the year and terms of the agreement with Elisabeth that the attack broke, any pledge of the duchy 1411-1425, and the 1444 payment to Elisabeth.
